newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Belgacom 1996 net profit up 21 percent.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Belgacom 1996 net profit up 21 percent.

text.p: Belgian state telephone company Belgacom SA said on Thursday its 1996 group net profit soared 21 percent and it expected further growth before extraordinaries in 1997.
"The Belgacom group will continue efforts to improve its competitive position in view of total deregulation of the telecoms market on January 1, 1998," it said in a statement.
It made net profits of 13 billion Belgian francs ($371.9 million) in 1966 on turnover up 9.1 percent to 138.7 billion francs. The figures confirmed provisional data released in January.
Belgacom said its turnover reflected growth in mobile telephony, its national telephone service, subscription fees and in international telephone business.
Belgacom is 49-percent owned by a consortium comprising Ameritech, Singapore Telecom, TeleDanmark and three Belgian investors. The remaining shares are held by the Belgian state.
At the end of 1996 Belgacom had 4.67 million fixed line connections, up slightly from 4.63 million at the end of 1995. This represented a penetration rate of 46 percent, it said.

The company's mobile telephone unit Belgacom Mobile SA -- 25 percent owned by U.S. AirTouch Communications Inc -- currently had a total of 440,000 customers, a rise from 410,172 at the end of 1996 and 235,238 at the end of 1995. ($1=34.96 Belgian Franc)
